response:
Diagnosis. The archive has converged on one dominant recipe and one clear diagnostic split. Dominant: the research-commitment floor certified by a quality leg — SustainedResearchFloorCashBacked (fmb 4.47, α 4.7%, t 3.60, Sharpe 0.45) and CommitmentWithCashBackedEarnings (fmb 2.06, α 4.7%, t 3.29, Sharpe 0.39). These two use *different* certifications (level of cash flow vs. accrual-freeness of earnings) and both deliver ~4.7% alpha, which suggests the certifications are partly substitutes and the binding one should be identified. Diagnostic split: several gen-6 signals had strong slopes but no portfolio spread (CumulativeResearchRelativeToInternalCash fmb 3.73/α 0.1%; IntangibleBookBeyondLifetimeEarnings fmb −3.14/α −0.8%), and EconomicLeverageOverstatement returned a NaN alpha from its zero mass — the recurring lesson being that measures whose extremes are populated by near-zero-denominator or exactly-zero firms cannot form tradeable legs, even when the middle of the cross-section is informative. With two generations left I consolidate the commitment family, pair slope-strong short-side legs with alpha-strong ones, and fix the two coverage-limited channels on a wider accounting basis.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: BindingCertificationOfCommitment
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5)), MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 3)))))
HYPOTHESIS: A sustained research program is credible only if it passes *both* funding tests — the firm generates substantial operating cash flow and its reported profits are not accrual illusions — so the weaker of the two certifications should govern. A firm with strong cash flow but accrual-inflated earnings, or clean earnings but thin cash generation, is only as credible as its weakest leg.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive's two best-alpha long signals share the same commitment leg but use different certifications and each earned 4.7% alpha, so the open question is whether the certifications are substitutes (in which case the binding-constraint form adds little) or complements (in which case taking the minimum sharpens both tails). Using MIN of the two quality ranks rather than a triple product avoids the compression-toward-zero problem the critic identified for stacked rank products, because the certification factor remains a well-spread [0,1] variable.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: CommitmentWithKnowledgeProfitYield
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ib, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Commitment without productivity is waste: among firms that sustain a research program, the ones worth owning earn high profit per dollar of accumulated research, meaning the knowledge stock is converting into bottom-line income rather than absorbing it indefinitely.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive has certified commitment with funding capacity (cash-flow level, accrual quality, margin floors) but never with *research efficiency*, and earlier attempts at intangible-yield ratios failed because they used within-firm own-history ranking or fragile cash-flow-per-intangible-dollar denominators without any commitment leg to anchor the sample. Pairing the yield with the commitment floor keeps intangible intensity in the leading position that has consistently worked, while winsorized industry ranks contain the small-stock denominator tail.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: UnearnedIntangibleBookWeakCoverage
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(SUB(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), at), RATIO(re, at))), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, lt), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: The dangerous configuration on the short side is an intangible book that exceeds lifetime accumulated earnings — growth that was bought rather than earned — held by a firm whose operating cash flow covers little of its total obligations; such firms must write down assets they never earned while servicing claims they cannot cover.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This deliberately pairs the two short-side legs whose evidence disagreed: the unearned-book measure produced the strongest slope in the archive's negative direction (fmb −3.14) but almost no alpha, while cash-flow-to-liabilities coverage produced the strongest short alpha (−4.7%, t −3.62) with a weaker slope, so their conjunction targets the joint objective rather than one metric. The interaction is economically specific to purchase-accounting risk rather than generic distress, because the first leg compares two stocks (acquired intangibles versus earned capital) that plain leverage or coverage sorts do not distinguish.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: OwnHistoryResearchIntensityWithEarningsQuality
EXPRESSION: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: Research intensity read against a firm's own five-year history separates programs being expanded or held at full strength from programs quietly being wound down, independently of how research-heavy the industry is; when a firm is at the top of its own research range and is also persistently profitable, the intangible investment is both committed and affordable.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The peak-normalized version of this idea produced one of the archive's best slopes (fmb 4.44) but only 4% coverage and modest alpha because dividing by the five-year maximum is undefined or degenerate for many firms; TS_RANK is bounded by construction, has no denominator, and pairs here with an ib-based quality leg, which should roughly triple usable observations. Comparing it with the level-floor version tells us whether commitment is best measured cross-sectionally or within-firm — the last open design question in the winning family.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: DoubleTroughCommitmentAndRestatedReturn
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5)), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Durable intangible productivity is a worst-case property on both sides of the interaction: research the firm never cut, and a restated return on knowledge-augmented capital that never collapsed. Firms clearing both floors have demonstrated that their innovation franchise survives the cycle rather than merely averaging well through it.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Both legs are individually validated — the commitment floor carried the best slope in the archive and trough restated profitability delivered α 3.6% at full 14.6% coverage — and because the restated ratio is ib-based this conjunction escapes the oancf coverage ceiling that confines the current leading signal to 9% of observations. It differs from the accepted gen-6 conjunction by replacing a three-year average of the operating-capital restatement with a five-year floor, so it tests whether downside quality dominates average quality inside the commitment family.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: EarningsValidationOfIntangibleCapital
EXPRESSION: IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(ib, 5), ADD(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: Intangible capital — acquired and internally built — must ultimately be validated by accumulated profit; five years of cumulative income per dollar of total intangible capital measures how much of that investment has been earned back, and unvalidated intangible bases signal both impairment risk and unproductive research.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The cash-flow version of this validation ratio has the best Sharpe in the archive (0.40, α 2.5%, fmb 2.87) but only 7% coverage because it needs five consecutive years of oancf; using cumulative ib doubles the usable sample and, unlike the ib+dp substitution rejected earlier, changes the accounting basis of the test from cash delivery to earned profit, which is the measure impairment tests actually reference. If the earnings version retains the slope and alpha, the final consolidation can use the wider sample; if it does not, we learn that cash delivery specifically — not accounting profit — is what validates intangible capital.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---CRITIQUE BindingCertificationOfCommitment---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The two "certifications" (MA(oancf/at) and NEG(MA((ib−oancf)/at))) are both monotone increasing in operating cash flow and therefore highly correlated, so MIN of their ranks will largely reproduce either archived signal (both already ~4.7% alpha) rather than test genuine complementarity — a near-cosmetic recombination of two existing results.

---CRITIQUE CommitmentWithKnowledgeProfitYield---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Research efficiency (ib per dollar of accumulated R&D) is a certification leg the archive has not tried, but note the mechanical tension that the yield leg is decreasing in R&D stock while the commitment leg is increasing in R&D intensity, so partial cancellation and heavy clustering of non-reporters at zero are real risks.

---CRITIQUE UnearnedIntangibleBookWeakCoverage---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The expression and expected negative sign are internally consistent and the design sensibly conjoins the archive's strongest short-side slope with its strongest short-side alpha, but with re/at and oancf/lt as the two ingredients it risks collapsing into a generic financial-distress composite (a well-documented anomaly) rather than a purchase-accounting-specific effect.

---CRITIQUE OwnHistoryResearchIntensityWithEarningsQuality---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: This addresses a genuine open design question (within-firm versus cross-sectional measurement of research commitment) with a construction fix that removes the degenerate TS_MAX denominator that crippled the earlier 4% coverage variant, though TS_RANK over five annual observations is coarse and degenerate for non-R&D firms.

---CRITIQUE DoubleTroughCommitmentAndRestatedReturn---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Economically coherent and the ib-based restatement plausibly lifts coverage above the oancf-constrained leader, but it is the third conjunction built on the same commitment-floor leg and the restated-profitability leg itself embeds R&D intensity, so incremental information over existing family members may be small.

---CRITIQUE EarningsValidationOfIntangibleCapital---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: This is a single-input numerator swap (oancf → ib) on an already-tested validation ratio family, and cross-sectional variation in the ratio is likely dominated by the inverse of intangible intensity in the denominator, so the coverage gain does not clearly justify it as a substantively different test.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: TroughSurplusAfterResearch
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5)), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(SUB(RATIO(oancf, at), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: The real funding test is not the level of cash flow but whether cash flow still exceeded the research bill in the firm's worst year: a firm that sustained a high research floor and *still* ran a positive post-research cash surplus at its cyclical trough has proven the program is affordable out of operations, while an equally committed firm whose trough surplus was deeply negative was financing research from the capital market.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: The certification leg is no longer monotone in cash flow alone — it is cash flow *net of* research spending, so it is decreasing in the very variable the first leg rewards, and only firms that are simultaneously research-intensive and self-funding can rank highly on both. That trade-off structure is what the previous version lacked: two legs that both rose with operating cash flow simply reproduced the archived signals, whereas this pairing tests the budget identity that the theme's credibility story actually asserts.
REASONING_END: n/a

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: CashGrowthVersusIntangibleBaseGrowth
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(SUB(GROWTH(TS_SUM(oancf, 3), 1), GROWTH(ADD(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3)), 1)), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: Validation of intangible capital is a race between two growth rates: if cumulative cash generation is expanding faster than the intangible base that is supposed to produce it, the investment is productive; if the intangible base is compounding faster than cash, the firm is accumulating unproven assets through acquisition or unproductive research and the carrying value will eventually be corrected.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This is not a numerator swap on the validation-level ratio: it compares growth *rates* of the two themes, so cross-sectional differences in intangible intensity — which the critic correctly noted dominate the level ratio's dispersion — cancel out, and what remains is whether cash delivery is keeping pace with intangible accumulation within each firm. Both terms are unit-free growth rates measured over the same three-year accumulation window, which keeps the difference economically interpretable, and winsorization contains the small-base tail.
REASONING_END: n/a
